conviction_note: The quarter is pre-framed: the company reaffirmed Q3 and FY27 on 2026-09-29 and set FY28 at ~$11.0B / ~11% / >=33% margin on 2026-10-13. The reaction therefore turns on cRPO and the Q4/FY28 guide against a market that cut ServiceNow 27% on a 50bp cRPO guide shortfall. A sold-down sector, ~3 points of outperformance against IGV and a beat-and-maintain base case give a slight upward lean (p_up 52), with abs_move kept at the option-implied ~8.5 because the next guide is in this release. impact_sum +1.2 against a scaled +0.34: the findings are small positives on the company's own reaffirmations, set against a peer reaction function that punishes bookings guides. The gap reflects that one negative tail (a cRPO or FY28 cut) is larger than any single positive.

No street figure found for Q3 subscription revenue or cRPO, so the company guide is the bar.

A beat on Q3 subscription revenue alone is the base case.

next_guide.company_current_guide: FY27 subscription revenue $9.940-9.950B (+13%), non-GAAP operating margin 31.0%, FCF ~$3.18B; Q3 subscription revenue $2.515B, margin 30.0%, cRPO +11-12% (2026-08-27, reaffirmed 2026-09-29). FY28 framework ~$11.0B subscription (~11%) and >=33% non-GAAP margin (2026-10-13 analyst day).
next_guide.basis: Management restated the FY28 framework six weeks before the print and reaffirmed Q3/FY27 one month into the quarter. The 2.5% headcount cut supports the margin side. A raise is unlikely because the CFO has said AI upside is 'not all factored into FY28' rather than promising it, and a cut is unlikely given how recently the framework was restated, so maintain is the modal outcome. The tail risk is a cRPO guide below the street, the ServiceNow pattern.

findings.finding: Q3 subscription revenue is guided at ~$2.515B (+12%). Workday beat its own subscription guide by ~0.65% in Q2 ($2.471B against $2.455B), so the modal print is ~$2.53B, a beat of ~$15M inside the normal pattern. The market treats this as the base case.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Subscription beats with a margin raise bought +5.16% (2026-05-21) and +5.76% (2026-08-27). The same kind of beat was sold -7.85% on 2025-11-25 when the next guide underwhelmed.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: a beat of this size is what the market expects (Earnings Whispers' whisper is 3% above EPS consensus). If a larger beat were priced, the stock would not sit 11% below the mean target with a sector at lows.
findings.independence: Q1 FY27 also beat: subscription revenue $2.354B, +14.3% (https://newsroom.workday.com/2026-05-21-Workday-Announces-Fiscal-2027-First-Quarter-Financial-Results). Same company, different quarter.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-29, about one month into the Aug-Oct quarter, Workday filed an 8-K (item 2.02) announcing a 2.5% workforce cut ($65-80M charges, mostly in Q3) and reiterated its Q3 and FY27 guidance except GAAP operating margin. This is a mid-quarter reaffirmation that lowers the odds of a Q3 subscription or margin miss.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock rose +0.68% on that 8-K (baseline, 2026-09-29). Workday has not missed its subscription guide in the four prints sourced here.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for eight weeks, so mostly priced. What it adds is that the downside tail on the reported quarter is thinner than the 8.8% implied move suggests, but the option market still prices a wide move because the reaction turns on the forward guide.
findings.independence: Restructuring detail confirmed by https://www.panabee.com/news/workday-announces-2-5-workforce-reduction-and-80-million-restructuring-charge (secondary reading of the same 8-K, so one document).

findings.finding: At the 2026-10-13 analyst day, six weeks before the print, management framed FY28 at ~$11.0B subscription revenue (~11% growth) with >=33% non-GAAP operating margin and AI at ~70% of FY28 incremental ARR. A recently restated framework makes 'maintain' the likely next guide; the Q4 subscription guide implied by FY27 is $2.600-2.610B (+10.2-10.6%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide decides this stock: -7.85% on 2025-11-25 (uninspiring Q4 outlook), an 8% after-hours drop on 2026-02-24 on the FY27 guide (closed +2.24% next day per baseline), and +5.76% on 2026-08-27 when the margin guide was raised and FY28 framed.
findings.why_not_priced: The framework is public. What is not priced is how likely management is to repeat it unchanged: with ServiceNow's cRPO guide punished, the market's put bid and the 11% discount to the mean target price some chance of an FY28 cut. Management restated the framework six weeks ago, so that chance is lower than the setup implies.
findings.independence: The CFO on the Q2 call said FY28 growth matches the H2 FY27 rate of ~11% with at least 2 points of margin expansion, and that AI upside is 'not all factored into FY28' (https://www.webull.com/news/15497663744238592). Different date, same company.

findings.finding: Q3 cRPO is guided at +11-12%, down from +14.2% in Q2. The CFO cited lapping Paradox (over a point of last year's Q3 cRPO growth) and 'a continued mix shift towards customer-base bookings versus net new'. cRPO is the line software peers were punished on this season.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: cRPO +14.2% with an FY28 frame bought +5.76% in Aug 2026. The Nov 2025 print fell -7.85% when backlog and the Q4 outlook did not reaccelerate.
findings.why_not_priced: The deceleration itself is guided and known. The unpriced part is whether the new-logo mix shift keeps cRPO at the bottom of the range: an 11% print would read as no AI acceleration, which is what the Earnings Whispers framing says the market is looking for.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers notes seat counts at existing customers are roughly flat (https://finviz.com/news/423401/workdays-promised-second-half-ai-bookings-surge-faces-its-first-real-test).

findings.finding: ServiceNow beat Q3 cRPO ($13.65B, +20.5%, against $13.56B expected) but guided Q4 cRPO growth to 18.5% against ~19% expected and fell 26.9% on 2026-10-29. WDAY fell 4.4% the same day (204.36 to 195.46). The market's reaction function this season punishes even a small forward-bookings guide shortfall after a beat.
findings.link: Both are large-cap enterprise subscription platforms reported on cRPO, sold to the same CIO/CHRO budgets, priced on seats and moving to AI/consumption pricing; ServiceNow's HR Service Delivery competes with Workday in HR workflows. Same 'SaaSpocalypse' multiple: WDAY moved -4.4% on NOW's print day.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: WDAY fell on peers' AI-disruption days: -4.4% on 2026-10-29 and -5.8% on 2026-11-17 (https://www.trefis.com/stock/wday/articles/626295/what-just-happened-to-workday-stock/2026-11-18).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced in WDAY's -4.4% that day and the 8.8% implied move. The reaction-function lesson is a skew: a guide that merely holds may not be rewarded, and a light cRPO guide could be punished more than the history median. The option skew is only mildly put-bid (+1.18), which suggests the asymmetry is not fully in the price.
findings.independence: William Blair and TD Cowen comments in the same article; https://www.trefis.com/stock/now/articles/621796/what-did-servicenows-quarter-change-for-its-stock/2026-11-01 (separate outlet, same event).

findings.finding: HCM peers on the same quarter: ADP's US pays-per-control grew 2% (ahead of plan) and its FY PPC outlook was raised to ~1% (2026-10-28). Paycom grew revenue 10% and beat EPS 16.6%, but on cost discipline rather than demand (2026-11-04). Paylocity grew 10.7% and beat. Employment bases are stable to slightly growing and HCM demand is steady but not accelerating.
findings.link: Workday prices HCM subscriptions per employee (full-service-equivalent), so customer employment levels drive renewals and upsell. ADP pays-per-control measures the same US employment base. Paycom and Paylocity sell HCM/payroll to the same buyer, though mostly to smaller employers than Workday's enterprise base; no shared-revenue figure.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not measured for WDAY on peer HCM prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Public and small; it mainly removes the 'seat compression from layoffs' downside story for the quarter. If the market feared a seat collapse, WDAY would trade with the payroll names after their prints, and it did not.
findings.independence: Paycom: https://finviz.com/news/416401/paycoms-margin-surge-powers-a-166-beat-and-second-straight-raise-but-revenue-growth-isnt-speeding-up (2026-11). These are separate companies but a proxy, not Workday's own number.

findings.finding: SAP's Q3 2026 (2026-10-21) current cloud backlog was €24.1B, +26% at constant currency, with Q4 cloud growth guided ~23%. Enterprise cloud ERP/HCM budgets are being spent, though SAP is a share competitor of Workday.
findings.link: SAP SuccessFactors and S/4HANA Cloud compete head-on with Workday HCM and Financials for the same large-enterprise budgets; SuccessFactors is not broken out.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for a month; the read-across is ambiguous (budget health against share loss), so it is sized near zero.

findings.finding: Price path into the print: WDAY ran from $186 at the 10-13 analyst day to $210 on 10-22, then fell 17% to $173.36 on 11-19 amid sector selloffs (NOW print, 11-17 software rout as CRM fell 9.5%). It is still 3.3 points ahead of IGV over 20 days, 11% under the $206.78 mean target, and was +4.1% intraday on the print day. Sentiment is 'bearish but softened'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: From a sold-down setup (Apr 2026 low $112.5), the next two prints rose +5.16% and +5.76%. From the Nov 2025 high ($233.69), the Q3 print fell -7.85%.
findings.why_not_priced: The run-down is sector-driven: Trefis found no company news behind the 11-17 drop. That lowers the bar for a beat-and-maintain to be bought. The +4.1% print-day bounce spends part of that cushion, and the elevated short interest (6.7 days in July) adds a squeeze channel on a clean print.

findings.finding: The EPS whisper is $2.83 against $2.74 consensus (+3%). Workday beat EPS by ~5% in Q2 ($2.75 against $2.62), so the buy-side EPS bar sits roughly at a normal beat and EPS is not the line this stock trades on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS beats were bought in May and Aug 2026 and sold in Nov 2025; the guide decided each.
findings.why_not_priced: Priced: a whisper is the market's bar by definition.

findings.finding: KeyBanc downgraded WDAY to Sector Weight (stock -3% on the day, ~2026-10-16), arguing AI contribution is very early and HR IT budgets take a back seat to enterprise AI spending.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: -3% on the downgrade day; no print-reaction history on this item.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced (the -3% that day). The thesis (HR budgets deprioritised) would show in cRPO, which the cRPO finding already carries, so this is kept tiny to avoid counting it twice.
findings.independence: AAII: one downgrade and no upgrades in the month to 2026-11-12 (https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/539603-why-workday-inc8217s-wday-stock-is-down-503).

findings.finding: AI traction disclosed inside the quarter: agentic AI ARR ~$600M (from ~$150M a year earlier), ~25% of existing customers buying paid AI (from ~10%), just under 300 Flex Credit customers (nearly 200 added in Q2), and AI expected to exceed core in customer-base selling mix by year-end. Management said some AI growth is 'built into the back half'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The AI ARR disclosure accompanied the +5.76% Aug print; the analyst day was followed by a +13% run over nine sessions (partly reversed).
findings.why_not_priced: The numbers are public, but the market discounts AI ARR because consumption (Flex Credits) delays revenue recognition and the KeyBanc view says it is early. A visible step-up in AI ARR or ACV mix (above 25% of new ACV) would be news against a bar that, after NOW, expects little.
findings.independence: Q2 call: AI ARR 'roughly $600 million', 'just over 200' Flex Credit customers (https://www.webull.com/news/15497663744238592); Quartr analyst day summary (https://quartr.com/events/workday-inc-wday-analyst-day-2026_3YjWCEc5).

findings.finding: The 2.5% workforce reduction (mostly Product & Technology) carries $65-80M of restructuring charges, mostly in Q3, excluded from non-GAAP. The run-rate savings support the 30.0% Q3 margin guide and the >=2-point FY28 margin expansion.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin raises accompanied +5.16% and +5.76% prints; GAAP charges have not moved this stock.
findings.why_not_priced: The charge is non-GAAP-excluded and the margin path is already in the FY28 framework, so this is sized as a one-off.
findings.independence: Same 8-K as the reaffirmation finding (https://www.newsquawk.com/headlines/workday-wday-cuts-workforce-by-25-reiterating-fy27-and-q3-guidance): one document.

findings.finding: In Q2 Workday repurchased ~9.8M shares for $1.3B and the board authorised an additional $4.0B. Q3 buybacks lower the share count behind non-GAAP EPS.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The buyback was announced with the +5.76% Aug print; not separable.
findings.why_not_priced: Known; it supports EPS against the whisper but the stock trades on subscription and cRPO.

baseline_tension: Mostly agrees: a mild put skew (+1.18) and a -10.7% 20-day run-up sit beside sourced company reaffirmations that make a beat-and-maintain the base case. The one strong disagreement is the peer reaction function (NOW -27% on a 50bp cRPO guide shortfall), which argues the skew is too mild. Net, p_up sits only 2 points above 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (inside the guided range): Q3 subscription beat cut from +0.5 to +0.3 and the mid-quarter reaffirmation from +0.3 to +0.2; both land inside the company's own guide.
Lessons 6 and 7 (guided line, crowded short): the cRPO deceleration negative cut from -0.5 to -0.3; it is guided, and short interest was 6.7 days to cover at the last available settlement.
Lessons 5 and 7 (peer proxy, negative against an elevated short): the ServiceNow reaction-function negative cut from -1.0 to -0.7.
Lesson 2 (one-offs): the restructuring savings item cut from +0.2 to +0.1, and the buyback from +0.2 to +0.1 since the stock does not trade on EPS.
KeyBanc downgrade cut from -0.2 to -0.1: already priced, and its thesis is carried by the cRPO finding (no double count).
abs_move_pct (8.5) and p_up (52) left unchanged; the next-guide, AI, HCM-peer, SAP, price-path, whisper and Honeydew findings left unchanged.
